label: A0 poster
size_source: ISO 216:2007 A series. The whole series is derivable: A0 is 841 x 1189 mm and each next size is the previous one halved across its long side. verify_iso_series in the test suite recomputes it
what_it_does_not_tell_you: Nothing about where it hangs. 10 m is the distance an A0 is usually first seen from in a corridor or a lobby, not a property of the sheet. Measure the actual place and pass --distance

label: A1 poster
size_source: ISO 216:2007 A series
what_it_does_not_tell_you: A1 in a shop window is read from the pavement, which can be 2 m or 8 m depending on the setback. The setback decides the type size, not the paper

label: A2 poster
size_source: ISO 216:2007 A series
what_it_does_not_tell_you: 3 m assumes a wall. The same sheet on an easel at a counter is read at 1 m and carries three times the copy

label: A3 notice
size_source: ISO 216:2007 A series
what_it_does_not_tell_you: A3 is the size a queue reads while waiting, so the distance is set by where the queue stands

label: A4 flyer or one-pager
size_source: ISO 216:2007 A series
what_it_does_not_tell_you: Held, so the distance is arm's length and the legibility question stops binding. What binds instead is how much a person reads before putting it down, which no formula here answers

label: B1 poster
size_source: ISO 216:2007 B series. B0 is 1000 x 1414 mm and halves the same way
what_it_does_not_tell_you: B sizes exist because they sit between A sizes. Which one a Vietnamese printer stocks is a question for the printer

label: B2 poster
size_source: ISO 216:2007 B series
what_it_does_not_tell_you: See b1-poster

label: Bang ron / horizontal street banner
size_source: 0.8 x 3 m is the best-attested hemmed street banner: two Vietnamese print shops publish it in the same ngang list (bangronsukien.vn, invietnhat.vn, read 2026-08-04). No TCVN covers any OOH format and no decree sets a maximum - one vendor claims a Ministry of Culture limit and cites nothing, so no regulatory ceiling is encoded here. Other quoted ngang sizes are 600x2000, 1000x4000, 1000x5000 and 1000x6000 mm
what_it_does_not_tell_you: Nothing about whether you may hang it. Placement, permit and duration for outdoor advertising are governed separately and this repository has not researched them - see the poster-and-banner reference for the gap and what to bring back. Zero bleed because the edge is hemmed or eyeleted, so ink at the trim is lost in the fold. Bleed is 0 and the allowance is 50 mm, which is a different thing: bleed is artwork you let the blade cut, allowance is material the shop folds, sews or punches through and consumes. Nothing may be inside it. A pole sleeve (xo cay) needs 100 mm on the top edge instead of 50, single vendor.

label: Phuon / vertical street flag
size_source: 0.8 x 2 m appears in two vendors' doc lists alongside 0.6 x 1.6 m (bangronsukien.vn, invietnhat.vn, read 2026-08-04). Trade convention, no standard
what_it_does_not_tell_you: A vertical flag is read side-on more often than head-on, and this table has no term for viewing angle. A glance measurement taken head-on is the best case. 50 mm of material allowance every side for the hem and the eyelets, on two vendors' word. It is consumed, not printed to.

label: Standee
size_source: 0.6 x 1.6 m is published by three independent Vietnamese shops (innhanhthuduc.com, instandee.vn, onepidesign.com, read 2026-08-04), as is 0.8 x 1.8 m. Three shops agreeing is not a standard - nothing is standardised here - but it is what the word means on a quote
what_it_does_not_tell_you: A standee is passed rather than faced, so the top third is read and the bottom third often is not. The formula sizes type; it does not know that the price at ankle height is invisible The 50 mm allowance is the roll-up cassette: one vendor states 30 to 50 mm top and bottom, and 50 is carried because under-allowing loses artwork while over-allowing costs a strip of vinyl. An X-frame standee eyelets instead and the number is the frame's, not the file's.

label: Backdrop / phong nen
size_source: Sized to the venue's frame, so there is no default. Ask the venue for the frame's internal dimensions and the rigging allowance, and design to those
what_it_does_not_tell_you: The distance that matters for a backdrop is usually the camera's, not the audience's. A logo legible to the room can still be unreadable in the photograph that gets published

label: Table tent / standing card
size_source: A common quoted size. Unverified
what_it_does_not_tell_you: Read while seated and while doing something else. The constraint is competing attention, which this unit does not measure

label: Wall menu board
size_source: A common shop-fitted size. Unverified, and in practice cut to the wall
what_it_does_not_tell_you: menu-design.md and menu-engineering.md own what goes on it. This row only settles how big the type has to be

label: Bang quang cao tam lon / roadside billboard
size_source: Every OOH vendor publishes its own inventory dimensions and its own artwork template with its own bleed and eyelet allowance. There is no generic size and a generic file gets rejected. Ask for the site's spec sheet by site code
what_it_does_not_tell_you: 60 m is a placeholder for a road. The real distance is set by approach geometry, lane, speed limit and what obstructs the sightline, and only a site visit or the vendor's own sightline drawing settles it. Permit law is unresearched here

label: LED frontage or in-store screen
size_source: Pitch and panel count decide the pixel canvas, so the vendor's own spec is the only source. A file authored at the wrong pitch is resampled by the controller and the type goes soft
what_it_does_not_tell_you: An LED wall has a minimum legible type size set by pixel pitch as well as by distance, and pitch is not in this table. Ask for the pitch in millimetres and treat one pixel as one pitch unit

label: 300 x 250 display unit
size_source: 300 x 250, 728 x 90, 320 x 50, 300 x 600 and 970 x 250 are the sizes every ad server accepts and every publisher lists. This repository has not fetched a primary specification for them, so they are recorded as trade-common rather than cited
what_it_does_not_tell_you: A display unit is not read at a distance, it is read at whatever distance the phone is held. The CSS reference pixel already encodes that, which is why this row needs no metres - see plan_poster.py --explain-units

label: 728 x 90 display unit
size_source: As web-medium-rectangle
what_it_does_not_tell_you: 90 px of height is about four lines of legible body text and nothing else. The format is the constraint, and no amount of art direction adds room

label: 320 x 50 mobile banner
size_source: As web-medium-rectangle
what_it_does_not_tell_you: 50 px carries one line at glance size. A layout with a headline, a price and a button in it has already failed and the arithmetic says so before the design does

label: 300 x 600 display unit
size_source: As web-medium-rectangle
what_it_does_not_tell_you: The tallest common unit, and the one most often filled with a stacked poster. Height is not permission: the measure is still 300 px wide, so a long headline wraps to four lines

label: 970 x 250 display unit
size_source: As web-medium-rectangle
what_it_does_not_tell_you: Desktop only in practice. Whether it renders at all on the placement you bought is check_channel_spec.py's question, not this table's
